content_html:
Build a website with drag-and-drop. Add plugins without trusting them.

Try it in one command:

npx create-wordjs@latest my-site

No PHP, no MySQL, no build step — it downloads a ready-to-run bundle, starts a single process, and opens the setup wizard in your browser.

🧐 What is WordJS?

WordJS is free, open-source software for building and running a website — a blog, a shop, a company site, a portfolio. If you've heard of WordPress, think "WordPress, rebuilt for today": you get a visual, drag-and-drop page builder, ready-made themes and plugins, and search-engine-friendly pages out of the box.

The difference is what happens when you install a plugin.

On most website software, every add-on you install gets the keys to everything — your database, your passwords, your files. One bad or hacked plugin can quietly wreck the whole site. It's the single most common way websites get breached.

WordJS is built so that can't happen.

🔐 The big idea, in plain English

Think about apps on your phone. A flashlight app can't read your bank messages unless you let it — each app is boxed off and has to ask permission for anything sensitive.

WordJS does that for website plugins. Every plugin runs in its own locked box (a separate, operating-system-enforced process) and starts with nothing — no access to your files, your database, your visitors' data, or the internet. It only gets a capability when you, the admin, grant it — and you see exactly what each plugin is asking for.

So a plugin that turns out to be buggy, greedy, or outright malicious stays in its box. It can't read your passwords, steal your config, or take the site down. That safety is enforced by the operating system itself — not by trusting the plugin to behave.

Every other major CMS runs plugins with full trust. This is the one thing they can't copy without breaking their entire ecosystem — and it's what WordJS is built around.

Building a page by dragging blocks and editing text right on the canvas — the visual editor ships in the core, not as a paid add-on.

✨ What's inside

🎨 Build

  • Drag-and-drop visual editor (Puck) with 30 blocks & edit-in-place text
  • Token-driven themes + a live customizer
  • 64 themes & 31 plugins, one-click install
  • Real SEO: server-rendered pages, sitemap, RSS, social cards
  • Media library with automatic AVIF/WebP optimization

🧩 Extend — safely

  • Every plugin in its own OS process
  • Ask-permission capabilities, default-deny
  • Install-time code scanner + one-click sha256-verified marketplace
  • WordPress-style hooks, filters & shortcodes
  • Import from WordPress (posts, pages, comments, dates)

⚙️ Run

  • One process to deploy, SQLite by default
  • Or split / multi-machine over secure mTLS
  • SQLite · PostgreSQL · MySQL/MariaDB
  • Automatic HTTPS (Let's Encrypt)
  • 2FA, API tokens, webhooks, metrics
See the full feature list

Plugin system & security (the core differentiator)

  • OS-process plugin sandbox. Every plugin runs in a separate operating-system process (child_process.fork) — its own memory and event loop — so a crash, memory blow-up, or exploit is contained by the kernel and never takes down the host. Plugins reach the core only through a permission-checked wordjs bridge (structured-clone RPC, no live host references, an exact method allow-list).
  • Install-time code scanner. Before a plugin can activate, its JavaScript is parsed and walked for dangerous constructs (eval, exec/spawn, dynamic require, sensitive modules, forbidden process access). It's fail-closed (an unparseable file is rejected) and runs on every plugin — no exemptions.
  • Ask-permission model (default-deny). A plugin's manifest requests scoped capabilities (database, filesystem, settings, users:read, email:provider, notifications:provider, network, …); an admin grants each one per plugin. A call works only if the capability is BOTH declared AND granted. First-party plugins are pre-granted what they declare, but hold no special privilege — same sandbox, same rules.
  • Kernel hardening on Linux (default-on). Each plugin child also runs as an unprivileged user with dropped capabilities, no-new-privs, PID/IPC/UTS namespaces, a read-only filesystem, and a seccomp syscall denylist. A plugin without the network grant is dropped into an empty network namespace, so it can't reach the internet or your internal services even at the kernel level. (Probe-gated, with a clean fallback where unavailable; Windows gets a Job Object memory cap; macOS relies on process isolation.)
  • Per-plugin data isolation. Each plugin gets only its own wjp_<slug>_ database tables and a secret-scrubbed view of config — core users/options/sessions and secrets are unreachable. On PostgreSQL/MySQL the database itself enforces this via a per-plugin low-privilege role/user.
  • Plugin & theme marketplace. A curated catalog of 31 first-party plugins and 64 first-party themes with one-click, sha256-verified installs through the same hardened, sandboxed pipeline as manual uploads. Sources are admin-configurable (point it at any HTTPS catalog); all catalog items are first-party today, with third-party submissions on the roadmap.

Authoring & content

  • Visual builder (Puck) — drag-and-drop editing, in-place rich text (bold/italic/links, a color picker with eyedropper, font family from your installed fonts, size, alignment), a searchable block inserter with reusable section patterns, and a device preview (desktop/tablet/mobile) that renders the canvas at true device width.
  • Real server-side rendering — public pages are React Server Components, so crawlers and first paint get the real content, per-page metadata (generateMetadata), OpenGraph/Twitter cards, JSON-LD, real 404s, and a no-JS search form.
  • SEO basics — semantic HTML, sitemap.xml, robots.txt, and an RSS feed.
  • Themes — a shared, token-driven CSS framework (--wjs-* design tokens) that auto-styles pages, plus a live customizer at /admin/themes/customize. A theme's optional server-side functions.js runs in the same sandbox as plugins.
  • Hooks, filters & shortcodes (WordPress-style), dynamic roles & permissions (database-driven), and UI in español / english / português.
  • WordPress (WXR) importer — upload a .xml export to bring over authors, categories/tags, posts/pages (with meta, term relationships, and threaded comments), preserving publish dates. Idempotent and re-runnable.
  • Backups — full-site export/restore with retention pruning, plus privacy-first analytics (no cookies, daily-rotated salted IP hashing) and a built-in cron.

Operations

  • Gateway — a clustered reverse proxy (one worker per CPU, auto-respawn), health-check eviction, an mTLS internal control channel, and SSE-aware proxying. It also acts as the cluster CA for multi-machine deployments.
  • Automatic TLS — Let's Encrypt via HTTP-01 or DNS-01, manual upload, or a self-signed dev fallback; renewal works in single-process mode too.
  • Databases — SQLite (default), PostgreSQL, or MySQL 8+/MariaDB, all behind one interface with a migration system to move between them.
  • Headless-friendly — scoped API tokens (Authorization: Bearer wjt_…, per-resource scopes), HMAC-signed SSRF-safe webhooks, and token-gated Prometheus metrics.
  • Native mail server — an optional, fully sandboxed first-party plugin: inbound SMTP, direct-MX delivery, and DKIM signing.

🚀 Deploy your way

The same codebase runs three ways — switch anytime, no data migration:

Mode What it is Best for
🧱 Monolith Everything in one process, one port The simplest deploy — a small VM or container
🔀 Split (default) Gateway + backend + frontend on one host Scaling services independently
🌐 Separate The three services on different machines, joined over mTLS Larger, distributed setups 
# The whole thing, one process:
npx create-wordjs@latest my-site          # then open the browser wizard

# Or, from a source checkout:
npm run install:all
npm run dev:mono      # monolith on http://localhost:3000
npm run dev           # or the 3-service split
Architecture & run-mode details 
graph TD
    User((User)) --> Gateway[Gateway :3000]
    Gateway --> Frontend[Next.js Frontend :3001]
    Gateway --> Backend[TypeScript Backend :4000]
    Backend --> DB[(SQLite / PostgreSQL / MySQL)]
    Backend --> Plugins{Isolated Plugins}
Loading
  • Gateway — clustered Node/Express reverse proxy: routing, load-balancing, health-check eviction, mTLS internal channel, SSE-aware proxying, and the cluster CA.
  • Backend — the core engine (content, users, roles, the plugin/theme system, mail, certificates, and the sandbox). TypeScript, compiled to JS for production.
  • Frontend — the public site and the Next.js admin, including the Puck visual builder.

Monolith runs the backend (with its isolated plugins) and the Next.js frontend in one process on :3000 — no loopback proxy, no cluster — while still handling TLS, security headers, compression, and SEO rewrites locally. Split runs them as three cooperating processes behind the gateway. Separate spreads those three across machines: create-wordjs gateway --host <ip> makes the first box the cluster CA and prints ready-to-paste join commands with single-use, role-bound tokens; each other box enrolls over mutual TLS with no cert hand-copying.

See the Separate-mode guide for the walkthrough.

Live API reference (Swagger/OpenAPI) is served at http://localhost:4000/api/v1/docs (admin only).

🧭 Project status

Beta · pre-production · primarily solo-maintained.

WordJS recently completed rounds of security hardening (fixing a CSRF bypass, committed secrets, and XSS sinks, among others). The plugin sandbox has had multiple internal red-team passes — but there is no independent third-party audit yet. An external audit is strongly recommended before any production or internet-facing deployment, and the residual risks are documented plainly in SECURITY.md and POSITIONING.md.

The whole ecosystem is first-party: the marketplace ships 31 plugins and 64 themes, but there's no third-party author community or public review pipeline yet. Use it to build, learn, and experiment — do your own review before trusting it with real data or real users.

🔒 Security

The plugin sandbox is designed to fail closed, with defense-in-depth layers (see What's inside and Security Architecture). Beyond plugins, WordJS ships TOTP two-factor auth with an admin-enforced MFA-by-role policy, JWT revocation, per-(IP + account) login throttling, constant-time secret comparison, origin-pinned CSRF protection, and SSRF-safe outgoing webhooks.

Before exposing WordJS to the internet: have it independently audited, rotate every secret, and set a strong gatewaySecret (the gateway refuses management endpoints while the default is in place). Found a vulnerability? Please follow the disclosure process in SECURITY.md.

Tech stack
  • Runtime: Node.js (≥ 20.9; Node 20/22 LTS recommended)
  • Backend: TypeScript — compiled with tsc for production, ts-node for dev
  • Frontend: Next.js (React 19)
  • Editor: Puck · Styling: vanilla CSS + Tailwind
  • Communication: REST + JWT + scoped API tokens + WebSockets/SSE
  • Gateway: Express + Node cluster, http-proxy, mTLS internal channel
  • Sandbox: child_process OS-process isolation + acorn code scanning + runtime require proxies + layered memory caps (cgroup / Windows Job Object / RSS-poll)
  • TLS: acme-client (Let's Encrypt HTTP-01 / DNS-01)
  • Database: SQLite (better-sqlite3 / sql.js), PostgreSQL (pg), or MySQL/MariaDB (mysql2)
  • Tooling: ESLint + Prettier, node:test, GitHub Actions CI
Run from source & backend scripts 
npm run install:all       # install root + sub-packages
npm run dev               # split: gateway + backend + frontend
npm run dev:mono          # or everything in one process, one port

Public site at http://localhost:3000, admin at /admin. First-run setup (database + admin user) runs in the browser wizard, or via npm run setup.

In production the backend is compiled (tsc → dist/) and run as plain JS. From backend/:

Script Purpose
npm run build Compile to dist/ (strict config)
npm run typecheck Strict type-check (tsc --noEmit), enforced in CI
npm test Test suite (node --test)
npm run lint / format ESLint / Prettier

CI (.github/workflows/ci.yml, Node 22) runs the strict type-check, the compiled build, a dependency license gate, unit tests, integration tests against real postgres:16 + redis:7 containers, and the frontend lint/type-check/tests/build.

🔮 Roadmap

  • 🧩 Third-party marketplace — open the catalog to community authors, where "sandboxed & reviewed" is a verifiable trust badge.
  • ☁️ Media CDN — S3-compatible object storage.
  • 🌐 Multi-site — manage multiple domains from one install.
  • 🛡️ More kernel hardening — building on the default-on Linux sandbox layer.

📜 License

MIT — see LICENSE. Third-party dependency notices are in THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md.

Built with care by a small, independent project. Contributions, bug reports, and security disclosures are welcome.

blocks.html_en: • OS-process plugin sandbox. Every plugin runs in a separate operating-system process (child_process.fork) — its own memory and event loop — so a crash, memory blow-up, or exploit is contained by the kernel and never takes down the host. Plugins reach the core only through a permission-checked wordjs bridge (structured-clone RPC, no live host references, an exact method allow-list).

sentences.zh: 操作系统进程插件沙箱。

sentences.en: Every plugin runs in a separate operating-system process (child_process.fork) — its own memory and event loop — so a crash, memory blow-up, or exploit is contained by the kernel and never takes down the host.
sentences.zh: 每个插件都在单独的操作系统进程 (child_process.fork) 中运行——它自己的内存和事件循环——因此崩溃、内存爆炸或漏洞被内核包含，永远不会导致主机崩溃。

sentences.en: Plugins reach the core only through a permission-checked wordjs bridge (structured-clone RPC, no live host references, an exact method allow-list).
sentences.zh: 插件只能通过权限检查的 wordjs 桥（结构化克隆 RPC、无实时主机引用、精确的方法允许列表）到达核心。

blocks.html_en: • Install-time code scanner. Before a plugin can activate, its JavaScript is parsed and walked for dangerous constructs (eval, exec/spawn, dynamic require, sensitive modules, forbidden process access). It's fail-closed (an unparseable file is rejected) and runs on every plugin — no exemptions.

sentences.zh: 安装时代码扫描器。

sentences.en: Before a plugin can activate, its JavaScript is parsed and walked for dangerous constructs (eval, exec/spawn, dynamic require, sensitive modules, forbidden process access).
sentences.zh: 在插件激活之前，它的 JavaScript 会被解析并查找危险结构（eval、exec/spawn、动态 require、敏感模块、禁止进程访问）。

sentences.en: It's fail-closed (an unparseable file is rejected) and runs on every plugin — no exemptions.
sentences.zh: 它是失败关闭的（无法解析的文件被拒绝）并在每个插件上运行 - 没有例外。

blocks.html_en: • Ask-permission model (default-deny). A plugin's manifest requests scoped capabilities (database, filesystem, settings, users:read, email:provider, notifications:provider, network, …); an admin grants each one per plugin. A call works only if the capability is BOTH declared AND granted. First-party plugins are pre-granted what they declare, but hold no special privilege — same sandbox, same rules.

sentences.zh: 询问-许可模型（默认-拒绝）。

sentences.en: A plugin's manifest requests scoped capabilities (database, filesystem, settings, users:read, email:provider, notifications:provider, network, …); an admin grants each one per plugin.
sentences.zh: 插件的清单请求范围功能（数据库、文件系统、设置、用户：读取、电子邮件：提供者、通知：提供者、网络等）；管理员为每个插件授予每个权限。

sentences.en: A call works only if the capability is BOTH declared AND granted.
sentences.zh: 仅当同时声明并授予该功能时，调用才有效。

sentences.en: First-party plugins are pre-granted what they declare, but hold no special privilege — same sandbox, same rules.
sentences.zh: 第一方插件已预先授予其声明的内容，但不拥有特殊特权 - 相同的沙箱，相同的规则。

blocks.html_en: • Kernel hardening on Linux (default-on). Each plugin child also runs as an unprivileged user with dropped capabilities, no-new-privs, PID/IPC/UTS namespaces, a read-only filesystem, and a seccomp syscall denylist. A plugin without the network grant is dropped into an empty network namespace, so it can't reach the internet or your internal services even at the kernel level. (Probe-gated, with a clean fallback where unavailable; Windows gets a Job Object memory cap; macOS relies on process isolation.)

sentences.zh: Linux 上的内核强化（默认开启）。

sentences.en: Each plugin child also runs as an unprivileged user with dropped capabilities, no-new-privs, PID/IPC/UTS namespaces, a read-only filesystem, and a seccomp syscall denylist.
sentences.zh: 每个子插件还作为非特权用户运行，具有删除的功能、无新权限、PID/IPC/UTS 命名空间、只读文件系统和 seccomp 系统调用拒绝列表。

sentences.en: A plugin without the network grant is dropped into an empty network namespace, so it can't reach the internet or your internal services even at the kernel level.
sentences.zh: 没有网络授权的插件会被放入一个空的网络命名空间中，因此即使在内核级别它也无法访问互联网或您的内部服务。

sentences.en: (Probe-gated, with a clean fallback where unavailable; Windows gets a Job Object memory cap; macOS relies on process isolation.)
sentences.zh: （探测门控，在不可用时提供干净的后备；Windows 获得作业对象内存上限；macOS 依赖进程隔离。）

content_html_zh:
通过拖放功能构建网站。 添加插件而不信任它们。

用一个命令尝试一下：

npx create-wordjs@latest my-site

没有 PHP，没有 MySQL，没有构建步骤 - 它会下载一个可立即运行的捆绑包，启动一个进程，并在浏览器中打开设置向导。

🧐 什么是WordJS？

WordJS 是免费的开源软件，用于构建和运行网站 - 博客、商店、公司网站、作品集。 如果您听说过 WordPress，请想一想“WordPress，为今天而重建”：您将获得一个可视化的拖放页面构建器、现成的主题和插件以及开箱即用的搜索引擎友好页面。

不同之处在于安装插件时会发生什么。

在大多数网站软件上，您安装的每个附加组件都会获得所有内容的密钥 - 您的数据库、密码、文件。 一个坏的或被黑的插件可能会悄悄地破坏整个网站。 这是网站遭到破坏的最常见方式。

WordJS 的构建就是为了避免这种情况发生。

🔐 用简单的英语表达的伟大想法

考虑一下手机上的应用程序。 除非您允许，否则手电筒应用程序无法读取您的银行信息 - 每个应用程序都被封锁，并且必须征求任何敏感信息的许可。

WordJS 为网站插件做到了这一点。 每个插件都在自己的锁定盒子（一个单独的、操作系统强制的进程）中运行，并且从零开始——无法访问您的文件、数据库、访问者的数据或互联网。 只有当您（管理员）授予该功能时，它才会获得某种功能 - 并且您可以准确地看到每个插件的要求。

因此，一个被证明是有缺陷、贪婪或完全恶意的插件会留在它的盒子里。 它无法读取您的密码、窃取您的配置或关闭网站。 这种安全性是由操作系统本身来强制执行的，而不是通过信任插件的行为来强制执行。

所有其他主要 CMS 都以完全信任的方式运行插件。 这是他们在不破坏整个生态系统的情况下无法复制的一件事——而这正是 WordJS 的构建基础。

通过拖动块并在画布上编辑文本来构建页面 - 可视化编辑器位于核心中，而不是作为付费附加组件。

插件系统和安全性（核心区别）

  • 操作系统进程插件沙箱。 每个插件都在单独的操作系统进程 (child_process.fork) 中运行——它自己的内存和事件循环——因此崩溃、内存爆炸或漏洞被内核包含，永远不会导致主机崩溃。 插件只能通过权限检查的 wordjs 桥（结构化克隆 RPC、无实时主机引用、精确的方法允许列表）到达核心。
  • 安装时代码扫描器。 在插件激活之前，它的 JavaScript 会被解析并查找危险结构（eval、exec/spawn、动态 require、敏感模块、禁止进程访问）。 它是失败关闭的（无法解析的文件被拒绝）并在每个插件上运行 - 没有例外。
  • 询问-许可模型（默认-拒绝）。 插件的清单请求范围功能（数据库、文件系统、设置、用户：读取、电子邮件：提供者、通知：提供者、网络等）；管理员为每个插件授予每个权限。 仅当同时声明并授予该功能时，调用才有效。 第一方插件已预先授予其声明的内容，但不拥有特殊特权 - 相同的沙箱，相同的规则。
  • Linux 上的内核强化（默认开启）。 每个子插件还作为非特权用户运行，具有删除的功能、无新权限、PID/IPC/UTS 命名空间、只读文件系统和 seccomp 系统调用拒绝列表。 没有网络授权的插件会被放入一个空的网络命名空间中，因此即使在内核级别它也无法访问互联网或您的内部服务。 （探测门控，在不可用时提供干净的后备；Windows 获得作业对象内存上限；macOS 依赖进程隔离。）
  • 每个插件的数据隔离。 每个插件仅获得自己的 wjp_<slug>_ 数据库表和配置的秘密擦除视图 - 核心用户/选项/会话和秘密是无法访问的。 在 PostgreSQL/MySQL 上，数据库本身通过每个插件的低权限角色/用户强制执行此操作。
  • 插件和主题市场。 31 个第一方插件和 64 个第一方主题的精选目录，通过与手动上传相同的强化沙盒管​​道进行一键式、经过 sha256 验证的安装。 源是管理员可配置的（将其指向任何 HTTPS 目录）；目前，所有目录项都是第一方的，路线图上也有第三方提交的内容。

创作与内容

  • 可视化生成器 (Puck) — 拖放编辑、就地富文本（粗体/斜体/链接、带吸管的颜色选择器、已安装字体的字体系列、大小、对齐方式）、具有可重用部分模式的可搜索块插入器以及以真实设备宽度渲染画布的设备预览（桌面/平板电脑/移动设备）。
  • 真正的服务器端渲染 - 公共页面是 React Server 组件，因此爬虫和首次绘制会获取真实内容、每页元数据 (generateMetadata)、OpenGraph/Twitter 卡、JSON-LD、真正的 404 和无 JS 搜索表单。
  • SEO 基础知识 — 语义 HTML、sitemap.xml、robots.txt 和 RSS feed。
  • 主题 — 一个共享的、令牌驱动的 CSS 框架（--wjs-* 设计令牌），可自动设置页面样式，以及位于 /admin/themes/customize 的实时定制器。 主题的可选服务器端functions.js与插件在同一个沙箱中运行。
  • 挂钩、过滤器和短代码（WordPress 风格）、动态角色和权限（数据库驱动）以及西班牙语/英语/葡萄牙语 UI。
  • WordPress (WXR) 导入器 — 上传 .xml 导出以引入作者、类别/标签、帖子/页面（包含元、术语关系和线索评论），并保留发布日期。 幂等且可重新运行。
  • 备份 — 带保留修剪的全站点导出/恢复，以及隐私优先分析（无 Cookie、每日轮换的加盐 IP 哈希）和内置 cron。

运营

  • 网关 — 集群反向代理（每个 CPU 一个工作线程，自动重生）、健康检查驱逐、mTLS 内部控制通道和 SSE 感知代理。 它还充当多机部署的集群 CA。
  • 自动 TLS — Let's Encrypt 通过 HTTP-01 或 DNS-01、手动上传或自签名开发后备；更新也可以在单进程模式下进行。
  • 数据库 — SQLite（默认）、PostgreSQL 或 MySQL 8+/MariaDB，所有这些都位于一个界面后面，并具有可在它们之间移动的迁移系统。
  • 无头友好 - 范围 API 令牌（授权：承载 wjt_…，每个资源范围）、HMAC 签名的 SSRF 安全 Webhooks 和令牌门控 Prometheus 指标。
  • 本机邮件服务器 — 可选的、完全沙盒化的第一方插件：入站 SMTP、直接 MX 传送和 DKIM 签名。

测试版·预制作·主要由个人维护。 WordJS 最近完成了多轮安全强化（修复 CSRF 绕过、提交的机密和 XSS 接收器等）。 该插件沙盒已获得多次内部红队通过——但目前还没有独立的第三方审核。 强烈建议在任何生产或面向互联网的部署之前进行外部审计，并且残余风险在 SECURITY.md 和 POSITIONING.md 中清楚地记录。 整个生态系统是第一方的：市场提供 31 个插件和 64 个主题，但还没有第三方作者社区或公共评论管道。 使用它来构建、学习和实验——在将其信任为真实数据或真实用户之前，请先进行自己的审查。

🔒 安全

插件沙箱被设计为失败时关闭，具有深度防御层（请参阅内部内容和安全架构）。 除了插件之外，WordJS 还提供 TOTP 双因素身份验证，以及管理员强制执行的 MFA 按角色策略、JWT 撤销、每个（IP + 帐户）登录限制、恒定时间秘密比较、源固定 CSRF 保护和 SSRF 安全的传出 Webhook。

在将 WordJS 暴露到互联网之前：对其进行独立审核，轮换每个秘密，并设置一个强大的 gatewaySecret（默认值到位时网关拒绝管理端点）。 发现漏洞？ 请遵循 SECURITY.md 中的披露流程。
